newsitem.title: RUSSIA: RUSSIAN MINFINS NUDGE DOWN, PROFIT-TAKING SEEN.
newsitem.headline: RUSSIAN MINFINS NUDGE DOWN, PROFIT-TAKING SEEN.

text.p: Russian MinFins nudged down on Friday following a fall in U.S. Treasuries, but the slip was slowed by news that Russia had reconciled more of its debt to the London Club of commercial-bank creditors, dealers said.
They forecast a fall in prices on profit-taking ahead of the U.S. July Producer Price Index to be announced on Wednesday and U.S. July Consumer Price Index on Thursday.

"At first we tried to fall following U.S. Treasuries, but it was merely a slip as Vnesh (debt) is very strong on the London Club news," a major Western bank dealer said, estimating the fall at about 0.25 basis points in light trade.

Earlier on Friday Russia's Finance Ministry said it had fully reconciled 70 percent of its eligible debt to the London Club, meaning one step nearer to the restructuring agreement closing had been made.
Vnesh debt firmed on the news and MinFins, another paper representing Russia's foreign debt, followed, dealers said.
Bank Imperial dealer Dmitry Kreines forecast a slip in the market next week as operators started profit-taking fearing the U.S. economic indicators would mean rising inflation.
If the figures are higher than expected, the Federal Reserve may decide to hike its interest rates, making investment in U.S. government paper more attractive than emerging markets debt.
Kreines said the market was now uncertain of what to do after a strong rise this week.
"We have climbed high enough, it is scary to buy," he said, adding there was very little trade.

MinFins' spread over U.S. Treasuries has narrowed sharply in the last few days, compared to other emerging market debt, but not enough yet for investors to withdraw their cash from the Russian debt, the Western bank dealer said.
